statuses.Demonstrated: The current material shows the whole observable. Either a theorem or derivation chain (Lean or paper proof) whose premises need no confirmation from the executable model: established mathematics, the OPH axioms A1-A3 and the declared basis, and premises the model demonstrates. Or a committed executable result of the model (main candidate Interval Echo) whose observer records exhibit the observable. For a premise: the executable model satisfies it, or it is established mathematics.
statuses.Conditional: Proved (Lean or paper), but at least one premise needs confirmation from the executable model that the current material does not supply: a physical attachment or identification, a regime, continuum or refinement assumption, or a realization of a structure on the native process. The row names those premises.
statuses.Partial: The material shows part of the observable: some of its clauses, a restricted domain or preparation, a candidate other than the main one, a computation without a theorem for the full claim, or a retrospective comparison. The summary states the covered part and the missing part.
statuses.Open: No result in the current material. The work is in progress.

rows.name: The Born rule
rows.summary: Lean proves the finite Busch-Gleason theorem: every nonnegative normalized valuation additive on coexisting effects is the trace against a unique density operator, in every finite dimension, without continuity axioms. Its load-bearing premise is operational effect additivity (PR-03); a cubic deformation agrees with every listed context of the static fixture and fails additivity, so the fixture alone does not force the trace rule. On one Interval Echo cell, native contacts implement every coexistent pair of complex effects on four encoded rails, including noncommuting and singular pairs. Sharp-read certainty, relabelling and untouched-port invariance then satisfy the Busch-Gleason hypotheses on that encoded sector, giving one density matrix per preparation; on the state (1,i,1,-i)/2 the held effects 0.35 and 0.22619048 are read at 0.35104 and 0.22593 in 262,144 records. Separate H and 2H readers count 733,238 and 1,466,903 of 2,932,736 starts against 1/4 and 1/2, excluding the cubic alternative (143/512, 35/64). The scorecard grades FT-BORN partial: the complex register and terminal sampling rule are declared, and additivity over the full event grammar of the model is work in progress.
rows.why: Observers who share effects must assign them consistent probabilities. With additivity on coexisting effects, the finite Busch-Gleason theorem leaves only the trace rule.

The Lueders update is repeatable and idempotent, and on the eight-context phase table the Lueders maps form a CPTP instrument. The selecting hypothesis (certain-state invariance) and the source realization of the instrument are premises. On Interval Echo a common pulse word, a sharp address read and its native inverse give repeatable projective instruments for both defect signs; a native swap after the read keeps every first-read effect and raises the repeat-label error to 0.09549 (vacancy) and 0.65451 (excess). The model therefore realizes Lueders and non-Lueders instruments with identical first-read statistics, and its terminal read is the declared projective pointer rule.
rows.why: An observer certain of an answer is not disturbed by asking again; that consistency condition singles out the projection postulate among all instruments with the same probabilities.

rows.summary: Under the declared repair law with a common faithful reference (PR-07), Lean proves that the mean entropy production of one repair step equals the relative entropy from the input to its repaired image, is strictly positive whenever the step changes a strictly positive state, and vanishes exactly on the fibre-conditional fixed points. rows.summary: On the forced abstract product Lie type u(1)+su(2)+su(3) the adjoint is (8,1,0)+(1,3,0)+(1,1,0) and contains no (3,2,-5/6) or conjugate X/Y generator, so the ordinary simple-GUT gauge-exchange channel is absent from the twelve-dimensional current algebra. rows.name: Unitary scattering
rows.summary: In every Hausdorff topological group, ordinary convergence of g^n forces g to be the identity (Lean/QFT/FiniteUnitaryScatteringNoGo.lean). No wave operator, S-matrix or physical scattering amplitude is constructed; this is work in progress.

A finite scalar action on the golden population has a unique ground state with population, action and tick supplied, and it is no reflection-positive vacuum of a cosmological release law.

A model must supply source Euclidean data or a physical preparation, an expanding geometry and clock, a map from the accessible field to conserved stress and curvature, and one matter, photon and metric transfer system with a stated likelihood; the required transfer outputs include P_m(k, z) and fσ8(z). rows.summary: No source-emitted H0. Retrospective: +0.67σ from Planck 2018 (−0.0045 ± 0.0067) and −1.19σ from ACT DR6 P-ACT-LB (0.0062 ± 0.0052). A running and isocurvature freeze FZ-17 is proposed and unadopted.

The radius-nine restriction bounds (0.000382, 6.656e-9) belong to a retired package.
rows.why: Measured: how much a local observer's readout changes as the federation grows. Insensitivity to far-away detail is locality under refinement.

rows.name: Relaxation to the stationary state (equilibration)
rows.summary: For the fair classical seam rule with independent attempts on a connected port graph at fixed load, the screen-microphysics paper proves (Theorem 'Stationary density and occupation records') that the uniform law on the fixed-number sector is the unique stationary law, with reversible generator Gz = −Lz/2; on the 66 binary words of total load two each seam kernel is idempotent conditional resampling and the uniform law is the unique stationary law of every positive-weight mixture. OPH-THERMO-FOUR-LAW-PACKAGE proves that relative entropy to the reference is nonincreasing under every kernel with that stationary law. Missing: a native Interval Echo preparation of the stationary state with an error bound uniform over untouched references; that result belongs to a retired package.
rows.why: Measured: how close a fixed-number sector gets to its stationary state under repair. Thermal equilibrium reached by repair alone is the starting point of the thermodynamic laws.

rows.name: Seam-current covariance and Brownian path limit
rows.summary: For the fair classical seam rule with independent Poisson attempts on a connected port graph, the screen-microphysics paper proves a Gaussian additive-functional limit: T^{-1/2}∫Bz dt converges to N(0, 4κ B L⁺ Bᵀ) for every fixed linear readout B, and a leaky record of local repair events has covariance within 3κ/d_min of 4κL⁺. Missing: the seam-current covariance through the recovered rank-three frame on Interval Echo. The values (4N/99)·I3 and action coefficient 99/8 appear only in the OL-A4 note of tracking/observation_ledger.json, without a current receipt.
rows.why: Measured: the covariance of time-integrated repair readouts and their random-walk limit. Random local repair averaging into isotropic diffusion is a seed of kinetic behaviour.

rows.name: Two-particle field statistics from incident-clock counting
rows.summary: Incident-clock counting, the four-read protocols on all 28,680 two-particle states of the 240-port federation and the density-1/3 feedback reversal belong to a retired package with no file in the current tree. Interval Echo patch clocks count accepted local repairs (PATCH-01, PATCH-08); field statistics read on those clocks are work in progress.
rows.why: Measured: four-read field statistics of two-particle states in an observer's own clock units. Effective field descriptions are stated in such units.

rows.name: Record statistics at unused time lags predicted from a reconstructed transfer
rows.summary: A one-cell Interval Echo patch reconstructs its transfer from anonymous calibration probabilities at one exposure: 30 seams, hop angle 0.0625 and a rank-three slow Gram. The reconstruction predicts 288 held probabilities at twice and three times the exposure to below 10⁻¹⁰ (PATCH-06). On the 20-cell federation, return records of a patch in cell zero give simultaneous 99% lower bounds on eight positive gap frequencies after 17 bookings. The seven-dimensional cyclic transfer of the earlier construction belongs to a retired package.
rows.why: Measured: record statistics at exposures not used in the reconstruction. An observer recovers a Hamiltonian-like transfer from its own records and predicts later readings.

rows.name: Defect flux class of every particle (6Y mod 6)
rows.summary: On all 32 occupation patterns of the declared five-level code C³ ⊕ C² with hypercharge diag(−1/3, −1/3, −1/3, 1/2, 1/2), exact arithmetic gives the flux class k = 6Y mod 6 with multiplicities (4,6,6,4,6,6) for k = 0 to 5: quarks in classes 1/5 and 4/2, lepton and Higgs doublets in 3, right-handed leptons and gauge fields in 0. The certificate checks the Z6 kernel, the Aharonov–Bohm phase exp(2πi fk/6), class conservation in all 16 reaction types of the register and class neutrality on every closed carrier. The fermion and boson grading uses the declared spin-doublet and antisymmetric-occupation premises. Unshown: that the protected defects of the native Interval Echo process carry this register; the scorecard grades all 17 Standard Model identifications Open.
rows.why: The protected defects of the repair network would carry exactly the Standard Model centre classes, which fix how each species sees colour and weak fluxes.

rows.name: Integer lift of the face register
rows.summary: The face-lift identities (lift mod 6 equal to the stored class on every face of stored cuts at levels 4 to 7, no nonzero total among 68,515,840 carrier states) were computed on stored runs of a retired simulator law; no file in the current tree carries them. The current defect-class package covers the class mod 6 and has no integer lift.
rows.why: An integer lift would assign each defect face a hypercharge value inside its centre class. Whether the lift is conserved inside a class decides if it labels particles.

rows.name: Lepton register phase (exclusive read count)
rows.summary: The 432-state register round, its 60-address cycle and the exclusive event fraction 2/9 belong to a retired package; the current tree describes them only in the lepton-family theorem-interface README, which links earlier commits. A dynamical and detector map from the travelling Interval Echo load to a register phase is work in progress.
rows.why: A register phase read from exclusive events would fix the family structure of the charged leptons on one source.

rows.name: Charged-lepton mass hierarchy (e, μ, τ)
rows.summary: The scorecard grades OW-11 (lepton mass spectrum) and the muon and tau identifications Open for Interval Echo. Comparison constructions on the written-field extension and its first-order cyclic guide are documented in the lepton-family package with their own preparations and controls. A derivation of the charged-lepton hierarchy on the main candidate is work in progress.
rows.why: Observers measure three charged leptons with identical charges and very different rest energies. Accounting for the hierarchy is a central particle-physics observable.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Exact directed seam write
rows.summary: The screen-microphysics paper proves that a stochastic seam rule that conserves the seam total, ends at minimal x_a² + x_b², breaks ties with a load-independent coin and is symmetric under endpoint exchange is the floor/ceiling rule with a fair coin. The native write of Interval Echo is the contrast-memory seam isometry; its classical strict branch is that rule with the theorem's load-dependent decrease of Σx_p² (FT-SEAM).
rows.why: Every record of a load transfer across a seam comes from this write. Observers who prepare definite loads read the floor and ceiling of the mean, with a fair coin for the odd unit.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Native repair selects and the candidate carries the rank-three Gram band
rows.summary: Under independent unit-rate seam attempts in a balanced binary sector the native rule acts on centred loads with mean generator −L/2, L = 5I − A on the 30 internal seams; the slowest band 5 − √5 has multiplicity three and projector G/4 (screen-microphysics paper). For Interval Echo the one-load Hamiltonian minus its common offset 48 equals L/2, and the Gram projector intertwines on all three directions with Frobenius errors below 3×10⁻¹⁶ (FT-BAND). Transport of a moving observer's full records is a separate test.
rows.why: The three slowest response directions of a cell are what an observer reading port loads finds as three spatial components.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Orthogonal local pointer records
rows.summary: The Interval Echo cell-patch clock reads a sharp material rail, repeated protected readings agree, and both owners reread the same physical digit in the projection test. For one fresh write in the 78-word total-two sector the reduced channel equals the record law E on all 6,084 matrix units; a total-sensitive control equals T, every sharp word agrees and 110 matrix units separate the two. The empty/full interferometer gives 786,711 bright returns of 1,048,576 simulated starts at phase π/3 against 524,560 for the control (FT-RECORD).
rows.why: Observers rely on orthogonal pointer records that a second reading confirms. The record also fixes which quantum coherences a repair keeps.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Disjoint finite operations preserve a remote marginal
rows.summary: Interval Echo seam gates and sharp pointer instruments act on their addressed registers, so a complete local operation preserves every disjoint marginal. On the 20-owner board the first public two-port record selects which of two enrolled seams receives the second echo and read; all 81 adaptive branches are complete on arbitrary private collar states, and the channel summed over records preserves every disjoint complementary marginal, also with a balancing charge reference in the fixed-total sector. Serving the same seam irrespective of the record changes the public law by total variation 1/2 on a sharp input (FT-LOCAL). The controller and protected windows are supplied; the finite operational support identifies no spacelike region.
rows.why: An observer whose registers a local operation does not touch sees no change in its own statistics, whatever the outcomes. This is the finite no-signalling condition.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Finite continuous free evolution
rows.summary: The free one- and two-load evolution of the Interval Echo patch instrument exponentiates the native Hermitian generator (PR-43 fulfilled for Interval Echo). After a fair reference exchange two material clocks have identical marginal modular rates; the joint reference predicts covariance +0.07465 ± 0.00304 at eight accepted pulses, the detectors measure −0.00002 ± 0.00121, and that reference misses 22 of 24 held joint probabilities while independent references with the same marginals cover all 24 (FT-FLOW). The flow parameter has no laboratory-time calibration.
rows.why: Between interventions an observer's records evolve under one continuous reversible flow. Its generator is what observers call the Hamiltonian.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Two-overlapping-patch information projection
rows.summary: On the 20-cell sphere two overlapping two-cell owners with a shared fair record and private mismatch probability 1/4 run 32 native branches per order in both orders; each owner's accessible table is (3/8, 1/8, 1/8, 3/8), the unique weighted projection to the uniform reference. Independent and common private errors give the same accessible tables and different external agreement, 5/8 and 1 (FT-PROJECTION).
rows.why: Two observers with overlapping patches each hold the least informative table compatible with what they share. Their records leave the joint coupling they cannot access undetermined.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Strict repair with an order-independent endpoint and a retained phase on an intercell wedge
rows.summary: A buffered two-request priority service on two Interval Echo cells tests absolute written contrast: it excludes balanced inputs, accepts only energy-lowering writes and gives identical channels under reversed arrivals. Relative-phase preparations give rail probabilities 0 and 1 at the winning address; the control that interrogates both seams gives 1/2 for both preparations (FT-STRICT-WEDGE). The full confluence contract PR-01 is partial for Interval Echo.
rows.why: Two observers repairing competing seams in either order reach the same endpoint, and a phase retained at the winning address stays readable. Order-independent outcomes make a shared record possible.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Faithful twelve-current response on the declared finite sector
rows.summary: On one Interval Echo cell the rotation-selected current service on each of the one-load and bound two-load sectors gives 12 independent visible closed directions; all 66 brackets and 720 covariance checks pass per sector. An extended service reaches 17 visible directions, and the 17-offer standard reproduces all twelve guarded directions on the binary pair sector (FT-CURRENT). The service is selected by the cell rotations; the complete physical menu of controls is unidentified.
rows.why: The twelve port currents an observer can drive and read form the finite current algebra from which the gauge classification starts.

rows.name: Three spatial directions in a field measured by observers (Interval Echo witness: blind recovery of programmed station directions)
rows.summary: On the programmed native scalar instrument anonymous one-period counts recover three binary station directions and predict 24 held clock-stopped distributions with largest absolute discrepancy 0.001022; dropping any recovered direction forces an error of at least 0.11377. Relabelled local ports recover a rank-three Gram, and on 20-, 80- and 320-cell screens neighbouring patches decode all 144 held three-sign preparations. The controller supplies the spatial routing and timing. Missing: three directions with independently ranged physical scales and refined stations; on a seven-station menu every board has a five-site subset whose measured ranges exclude a 3D Euclidean placement within 5% (OBS-02 Partial).
rows.why: Observers infer three independent directions in a field from timed patch records. A field with independently ranged scales in three directions is what space means operationally.

rows.name: Interval Echo · A fixed observer reads a material timing record
rows.summary: An Interval Echo patch retains both its latest primary repair outcome and a physical five-position hand. On 320 cells the patches posted 41,108 marks and retained 40,812 quiet opportunities under the supplied schedule, and all shared checkpoint readings agreed (PATCH-01). The source cadence and gate windows are supplied.
rows.why: A fixed observer reads time from a material register it holds. Every clock comparison starts from such a record.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Own-history clock transport and fixed-home reunion
rows.summary: A moving Interval Echo patch carries its hand, elapsed count and interval memory; at physical reunion both owners read home and traveller words through a shared local register. Two distinct hands agree on all 396 tested service opportunities, and the five-bit material profile represents intervals up to 31. On alternating 2- and 6-service handoffs the traveller/home ratio is 0.955354 ± 0.0019 (SE). Gate windows and movement are supplied (PATCH-02).
rows.why: Travelling and stay-at-home observers compare elapsed readings at reunion. This comparison is the operational content of a twin experiment.

rows.name: Interval Echo · A prepared excitation persists and is locally detectable
rows.summary: The idle-clock binary sector of Interval Echo is the reference contrast-memory interaction at κ = 8. After a local herald the same patch reads an intact pair again with probability 0.993226, against 0.338671 for exchange alone, and the reference prepared-pair theorem applies in this free sector (PATCH-03). The coupling κ = 8 is a declared parameter.
rows.why: Observers find objects that persist and can be detected again where they were. Particle stability is the first matter observable.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Propagation of a localized defect or bound excitation
rows.summary: On 320 cells Interval Echo patches tracked 34 conserved mobile doubles across 2,399 serviced transfers. Separately, a locally heralded free pair reaches another internal seam of its cell at the next read with probability 0.803077 (PATCH-04). The transfers follow a supplied service schedule.
rows.why: A local excitation identified at one place is detected elsewhere with its identifying property intact. This is the operational content of a moving particle.

rows.name: Smooth 3+1D description of a finite observer menu (Interval Echo witness: clocked scalar propagation on a programmed 3D chart)
rows.summary: The eight-station scalar instrument recovers a finite 3D chart from anonymous counts; at fixed bandwidth and bounded times its prescribed refinement converges to a flat 3+1D free Klein–Gordon propagator on this programmed sector. Missing: an independently refinable radial field with a shared clock and physical regional transfer. In free flight a source-free test with four calibrated anchors misses the 5% tolerance on every held echo path for both probes on 20, 80 and 320 cells, and the round radial product of the measured angular screen fails at 5% for every radial assignment on both station menus (PATCH-05 Partial).
rows.why: Observers describe their records as a smooth 3+1D spacetime with fields. A verified finite family of held four-dimensional predictions is the executable test of that description.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Three independent spatial response components in local patch records
rows.summary: A one-cell Interval Echo patch prepares and reads one load at twelve ports. From anonymous calibration probabilities the inverse infers 30 edges, a hop angle of 0.0625 and a Gram of rank three; twice and three times the exposure reproduce that subspace and 288 held probabilities below 10⁻¹⁰, and the best rank-two Gram has relative error 0.57735 (PATCH-06). The free sector is measured with the clock idle.
rows.why: An observer with a finite aperture infers how many independent spatial components its local responses have. Three is the operational dimension of space.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Three spatial response components reach neighbouring patches
rows.summary: Relabelled local ports recover a rank-three Gram. On complete 20-, 80- and 320-cell Interval Echo screens neighbouring patches decode all 144 held three-sign preparations sent by native evolution, and a short-range incidence survey with the frozen hopping scale predicts 72 further words at held senders and untested dwell times (PATCH-07). The signal is an occupation-probability contrast; timing and addresses are supplied.
rows.why: Three independently prepared components sent from one patch are decoded by its neighbours. The three spatial directions are shared between observers.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Two kinds of material hand agree on the same accepted repair events
rows.summary: On guided Interval Echo journeys a transported coherent oscillator and the registered event hand agree on accepted local repairs: both unequal-leg schedules meet the ±0.006 equivalence margin, and an equal-leg replication gives oscillator minus hand +0.000046 ± 0.000497 (SE). The matched raw-positive oscillator differs by +0.03204 ± 0.00044. The guide and gate schedule are supplied (PATCH-08).
rows.why: Two clock mechanisms carried on the same journey give the same elapsed reading. Agreement across mechanisms is what makes elapsed time a property of the journey.

rows.name: Interval Echo · Optically ranged reunion on held native links and motion schedules
rows.summary: A home patch measures a reciprocal light time, receives an arrival report and reads both elapsed words at one local reunion. The three-bit schedules 3/5, 5/3 and 7/7 and the five-bit 8/8 schedule meet the frozen ±0.004 band including four paired standard errors; the narrow three-bit 8/8 overflow control and the raw-primary controls disagree (PATCH-09).
rows.why: A home observer forecasts a traveller's elapsed reading from light-time ranging and checks it at reunion. This is the operational form of relativistic time dilation.

rows.name: Excess gravity predicted from retained patch records (Interval Echo witness: charge variance from two writes under one retained history)
rows.summary: On one written Interval Echo word equal untagged states give the same complete radar records. A material tag and word meter measure a between-history amplitude of 0.09156 ± 0.00037 nats; with two physical writes the patch measures their covariance, and an independent flying receiver detects the shared history at fixed ordinary load. Halving the amplitude on each write quarters the predicted arrival contrast. Missing: a physical reference, cut count, conversion to gravitating mass and a geometry calibrated on ordinary stress. The galaxy and lensing comparisons in code/cosmology/rar_deep_regime are retrospective and locate these gaps (PATCH-10 Partial).
rows.why: Observers attribute excess orbital and lensing signals to unseen mass. Predicting them from retained records with one source law tests a record origin of that excess.

rows.name: Guided three-family dispersion readout (constructed extension)
rows.summary: Executed on the first-order cyclic extension of Interval Echo, a written-field construction outside the registered law: a vacancy released on the twelve-port degree-six guide is counted at the first port for four relative source phases, and the data resolve three positive frequencies at each spatial wavelength. Two measured gaps per branch fix its dispersion coefficients; the fitted kinetic coefficient is A = 4 on all three branches and the largest held third-mode frequency error is 1.8×10⁻¹² exposure units. With the rest states held fixed, a unit cost at the terminal incidence grades raises the held-fringe RMS residual from 0.00069 to 0.479. Missing: the same readout on registered Interval Echo, an unconfined three-dimensional preparation, and a physical spin, conjugate and family identification of the three branches.
rows.why: Observers determine rest energy and kinetic coefficient of a moving excitation from its frequency gaps at several wavelengths. The readout method applies to any guided matter wave.

rows.name: Local charged preparation and distant recoil (constructed guide)
rows.summary: Executed on the first-order cyclic extension of Interval Echo: a vacancy starts one port from the source and its arrival selects a single port on 41.49% of trials. Two local interference filters select a rest line while the source contact is closed; six exposure units after release the signed detector eleven links away sees 37.41%, 37.46% and 32.09% of the three accepted preparations, and closing the middle contact removes every arrival. Fitting two wavelengths predicts the third gap at a fresh flight time within 1.3×10⁻⁸, and a scalar-register control gives one common line under all three family tags. Missing: the experiment on registered Interval Echo, a freely self-bound rest state, a physical spin and conjugate assignment, and recoil at a physical scale.
rows.why: Observers prepare a charge locally, release it and detect its arrival at a distance. Recoil read on the arriving charge ties its rest line to its motion.

rows.name: OpenWave 01 · Charge quantization
rows.summary: Interval Echo: two compact vacancy modes share one missing load across cells 5, 11 and 23 owner steps apart on the 20-, 80- and 320-cell boards, and paired contact reads distinguish that shared state from independent preparations with equal local means. At every free appointment the reduced state on either tested enclosing cut equals the filled host, and single and doubled loads both persist on empty hosts. The records select no topological electric unit and no law that excludes two half-charge daughters; the integer load is part of the carrier alphabet. Charge quantization as an outcome of the law, against a changed-law control, is work in progress.
rows.why: Every free charge measured is an integer multiple of e. A recovery has to produce the unit from the dynamics and exclude division of one unit into two half charges.
rows.observed: integer topological charge; e -> e/2 + e/2 excluded

rows.name: OpenWave 02 · Electron rest energy
rows.summary: Interval Echo, gateway-monitored compact vacancy on 20, 80 and 320 cells: with a material clock and six-seam storage, joint reads of two separated copies give exactly twice the one-copy energy, and a changed pair interaction shifts the two-copy reading, so the additivity test can fail. On the two-load preparation that carries an ordering phase, a calibrated boundary impulse produces a current predicted by an independent swap measurement (opposite-kick half-difference 0.00828 to 0.00838 at one clock unit across three placements, later adjacency reading at least 0.84319); an exchange-only comparator calibrated to the same formation energy gives a different recoil. Covered: dynamical holding of a localized state and a second use of its energy that can fail. Missing: identification of the held state with the electron, and an inertial mass read with its own ruler and momentum standard on the same excitation.
rows.why: The electron rest energy is the anchor of the charged-lepton sector; a recovery must select the state dynamically and let the anchored energy fix a second measured quantity.
rows.observed: 0.51099895 MeV from a dynamics-selected state, with a second quantity fixed by the anchor

rows.name: OpenWave 03 · de Broglie clock (Zitterbewegung)
rows.summary: Interval Echo: a sharp vacancy with monitored gateways gives a free internal beat at 2.237 and 2.232 per independently timed exchange unit on 80 and 320 cells, while the full blank one-vacancy spectrum lies in [32, 54] on all three boards, which excludes an internal frequency equal to the separately measured 35-unit vacancy transfer in that sector. On a unit-filled host one coin reading starts a free local beat on a written neutral seam at 31.995 and 33.001 in independent dimer-clock units, matched by separately resolved formation lines at 32.007 and 32.990; this is a stationary excitation gap. On the all-open 20-cell screen a bound pair of unequal loads carries its ordering phase to detectors across three owner boundaries. Covered: self-started internal oscillations read by observers. Missing: a frequency-rigid oscillation whose angular frequency equals an independently measured rest energy over hbar on one identified excitation; a uniform energy shift proportional to total load leaves every charge-preserving transcript invariant, so these reads leave the individual rest energy undetermined.
rows.why: Quantum mechanics assigns every massive particle an internal clock at its rest energy over hbar; a wave-mechanical model has to produce that clock on the same state.

rows.name: OpenWave 04 · Particle stability (Derrick escape)
rows.summary: Interval Echo on the 20-cell federation: two adjacent unit loads released with blank memories give an adjacent-pair reading in the launch cell with probability 0.98027 at kappa = 8 against 0.20291 with exchange alone at exposure 37; the cell-13 home-pair probability is at least 0.96325 through exposure 37, and a certificate bounds adjacency anywhere below by 5/6 at every exposure for adjacent launches on the stated federation class. Persistence that does not depend on kappa: a sharp single load prepared with three checked contacts keeps joint acceptance and home detection at least 0.999940596800 at every exposure on all 420 cells for every real kappa, and a two-load preparation with eleven written memories keeps home-seam probability at least 0.994771841 for every strength. OpenWave marked the historical pair Partial because kappa = 8 was chosen with the persistence result known; the single-load and written-memory filings are on HOLD. The prepared excitation carries no particle identification, which SM-e assesses separately.
rows.why: Particles persist under free evolution; a field model has to escape Derrick-type collapse or dispersal of its localized states.
rows.observed: particle state persists in free evolution

rows.name: OpenWave 05 · Magnetic moment μ (g ≈ 2)
rows.summary: Interval Echo: on each of the 420 owners of the 20-, 80- and 320-cell federations a compact vacancy eigenstate carries a stationary signed current. On 320 cells a tilted current vector precesses in a weak applied flux at 0.011053 per exchange unit (99% interval [0.010940, 0.011161]) against 0.011049 forecast from its zero-field moments. A probe confined outside the source cell records the same channel for either current and for no source, so no static exterior dipole field is measured. On a ten-port orbital belt, flux splitting and independent recoil give g_orb = 0.63327 [0.61951, 0.64710], which excludes g near two for that orbital. Covered: a stationary circulating current and its Larmor-type precession. Missing: a static dipole field from an identified stationary electron, g near two, and independent inertial-mass and spin standards.
rows.why: The electron carries a magnetic dipole with g close to 2 and precesses in a field; a model has to source the dipole from the particle's own circulation.
rows.value: precession 0.011053 vs forecast 0.011049 per exchange unit
rows.observed: static dipole B from internal circulation; g ≈ 2; Larmor response

rows.name: OpenWave 06 · Angular momentum J (spin ℏ/2)
rows.summary: Interval Echo: a signed defect transmits two coherent orbital modes across two cell boundaries on each native host; these modes are spatial orientations. The written-field Laplacian extension, a comparison law, transports a coherent orbital doublet with its four-face state, where intrinsic angular momentum is also unresolved. Field angular momentum of magnitude hbar/2 measured on an identified electron state is work in progress.
rows.why: The electron carries spin angular momentum hbar/2; a field model has to show that angular momentum in the field of the same state.
rows.observed: field-carried J = hbar/2 on the electron state

rows.name: OpenWave 07 · Spin-½ statistics (720° double cover)
rows.summary: Interval Echo, freely arriving signed orbital: a controlled full template turn and opposite orders of perpendicular half-turns give positive relative phase, and two addressed orbital packets exchange with +SWAP, while the same apparatus resolves imposed spinorial and odd-permutation signs; this orbital construction fails the double-cover test. Two commuting native half-turns on the twelve-port template give a negative relative order phase on the quarter of launches that pass both code filters, and one half-turn repeated twice gives positive phase. That sign uses a supplied filter and coherent reference, and a proved bound requires the two success probabilities of such anticommuting accepted unitaries to sum to at most one, which the measured code attains. A minus sign under a 2 pi rotation or a two-core exchange, read by interference against a symmetry-preserving control law, is work in progress.
rows.why: Fermions change sign under a 2 pi rotation and under exchange; this sign underlies the Pauli principle and atomic structure.
rows.observed: -1 under 2 pi rotation or exchange of two cores

rows.name: OpenWave 08 · Antimatter + annihilation
rows.summary: Interval Echo: observers prepare opposite phase walls on a closed four-dimer ring; during free registered evolution the walls disappear and energy reaches two radii on both sides. On three-dimer wings 8,245,757 of 268,435,456 launches give an ordered ring with excitation on both sides against 914 on the ordered sham. A local phase read after ordered-ring and two-mode filters gives a simultaneous 99% lower bound of 1.9574 on the two correlations against a separable limit of one, and supplied passive detectors on both sides take up energy on 36,025 wall launches against seven sham launches per 67,108,864 starts. Covered: annihilation of opposite order defects with correlated energy delivered into neutral material. Missing: identification of the walls as a charged particle and its conjugate, emission of radiation quanta, and the two- and three-photon positronium channels.
rows.why: Every charged particle has a conjugate with which it annihilates into radiation; positronium decays into two or three photons by its spin state.
rows.observed: pair annihilation into radiation; positronium 2γ/3γ follow-on

rows.name: OpenWave 09 · Neutrinos (neutral states)
rows.summary: Interval Echo, six-port annihilation receiver: the attached first gap is 31.80076 against a parent exchange energy of 65.00001 +/- 0.00015. Removing the source link with guards retained gives a soft line with gap 0.000945849, whose conditional frequency is 22.0% after a wall launch and 50.0% on the ordered sham; releasing the guards gives a first gap of 32.49358 with an analytic lower bound of 31.5. The soft line is present without the decaying source. A light, electrically neutral excitation produced in a decay is work in progress.
rows.why: Neutrinos are light, neutral particles released in weak decays; a model has to produce such states among decay products.
rows.observed: light charge-0 states released in decays

rows.name: OpenWave 10 · Neutrino oscillations (PMNS)
rows.summary: A flavour-tagged source, oscillation transitions and a mixing-angle determination on Interval Echo records are work in progress.
rows.why: Neutrinos are produced and detected in three flavours and oscillate between them with measured PMNS mixing angles.
rows.observed: three flavours, oscillation and PMNS angles

rows.name: OpenWave 11 · Lepton mass spectrum (μ, τ)
rows.summary: Interval Echo: for every net negative-unit composition of the registered blank-memory law, the ratio between host-referenced composition ground energies is bounded above by 57.5625, 203.296875 and 759.546875 on the 20-, 80- and 320-cell boards, which excludes a ratio of 3477 on those boards; on any finite refinement of the same architecture such a ratio needs at least 2319 defect ports in the heavier configuration. Three dressings on a ten-port belt give recoil and formation-energy ratios that disagree with each other. Three charged species with consistent recoil and formation energies are work in progress.
rows.why: Exactly three charged leptons exist, with rest-energy ratios near 1 : 207 : 3477.

rows.name: OpenWave 12 · Quarks
rows.summary: Interval Echo, ten-port belt: two polar probes covering the belt measure its integral total on moving period-three walls and same-load compact preparations, and subtracting the separately measured one-in-three bulk density gives identical fractional excesses. On parked three-wall preparations a remote six-dimer guide reads -0.3307 and +0.6656 ordinary units seven or eight seams from an end belt, and a common external material reference on the released 15-port ring gives +2/3 and -1/3 readings on the same stationary states as the triple detections. Covered: fractional material load carried by a partial winding of period-three order. Missing: electric charge on the winding defect against an independent electric standard and the identification of the string as a quark string; the charge reading depends on the smoothed periodic reference.
rows.why: Quarks carry charges of -1/3 and +2/3 of e; a model has to produce fractional charge as partial winding.
rows.observed: fractional charge as partial winding on a quark string

rows.name: OpenWave 13 · Baryons: bound state (p, n)
rows.summary: Interval Echo: an energy filter on one sharp three-load face selects the alternating arm level at 100.8894585 native units with 8.3645% start acceptance. On fully opened 20-, 80- and 320-cell boards the connected-triple probability exceeds 98.34% at every time after source admission, and at one exchange time the singlet fidelity on triplet admissions exceeds 99.92%. A calibrated period of the native material-number phase gives 36,326, 36,858 and 36,717 bright constituent reads with zero dark, where a 2/3 or -1/3 coupling would give 75% dark. rows.name: Integer port counting grammar and quadratic readback cost
rows.summary: Interval Echo ports hold 0, 1 or 2 loads, and the native seam write preserves total load and lowers the squared endpoint loads (FT-SEAM, Demonstrated). On the routed census a normal endpoint is exactly a quadratic-load minimum at fixed total load (FT-CONFLUENCE). Missing: the per-cell total-twelve sector appears only as a prepared unit-filled material, and no model result identifies the load square with the readback cost of public records. Selection ledger row 1; site row unit-port-split. Dictionary members: declared_integer_port_counting_grammar, declared_normalized_central_readback_quadratic_cost, declared_signed_event_and_conservative_repair_machine.
rows.statement: Port loads on a twelve-port cell are integer record counts with total load twelve, generated by signed append-only events and changed only by conservative whole-unit seam repairs. The physical readback cost of a load vector q is H(q) = sum_i q_i^2. Under these realization premises the all-one split is the unique minimizer, with floor 12 and gap 2.

rows.name: Compact-gauge refinement and transportable-sector receipts
rows.summary: Missing: a refinement tower of the native process with compact-group charge pullbacks and a transportable sector category. The nearest model result is the four-child isometry that intertwines the protected signed address algebra on all 100 parents of the 20, 80 and 320 cell tower (A2 evidence); it covers three levels of one address algebra and supplies no compact-group charge maps. Selection ledger row 5. Dictionary members: compact_gauge_refinement_receipt, finite_tensor_realization_receipt, zero_obstruction_bosonic_branch, transportable_sector_category. The completeness clause overlaps the source-complete character category of PR-46.
rows.statement: A cofinal refinement tail supplies finite-state extendability, center-compatible block-multiplicity embeddings, coherent surjective compact-group maps intertwining the stagewise representatives, and finite collar realizations of every tensor word and projector of the sector category. On the zero-obstruction strict-transport branch the seed carriers with trivial loop action generate the full rigid tensor category of finite-dimensional boundary-group representations, so Doplicher-Roberts and Tannaka reconstruction yield a compact gauge group.

rows.summary: Interval Echo has finite cap modular charges: on a prepared 79-state cap six charge variations agree with an independent weighted seam-energy meter, with supplied cap weights, filters and reference (G2, Partial). Missing: a refinement limit of native caps, round-cap rigidity and the geometric 2*pi normalization. Site row screen-s2 (theorem thm:conditional-cap-modular). Dictionary members: support_visible_BW_scaling, oriented_round_cap_rigidity, consistent_orientation_and_time_orientation, finite_cap_BW_certificate, independent_complete_MGNS1_certificate_on_the_same_tower. Related rows PR-23 and PR-42 state the 2*pi modular split for the first-law package and for horizon records; merge if the register treats cap normalization as part of PR-23.
rows.statement: On one cofinal refinement tower the support-visible geometric subnet emits nondegenerate oriented round caps with one sphere orientation and one preserved future null cone. The modular automorphism of each cap converges to its cap-preserving conformal flow with the 2*pi normalization, certified by finite cap Bisognano-Wichmann and mixed-GNS receipts on the same tower.

rows.name: Transactional commit contract of overlap repair
rows.summary: Interval Echo reaches a schedule-independent normal form on declared quotients without aggregate transactions: competing successful routed writes have the same census successor, and a protected coherent sweep orders conflicting visits by stored local priorities so that disjoint visits commute (FT-CONFLUENCE, Demonstrated). Missing: the aggregate-commit clauses on the native process and a quotient that keeps positions, signs, routing trees and the joint clock history. Dictionary members: semantic_dependency_complete_reads_and_revalidation, atomic_conflict_component_commits, coherent_canonical_union_collar_payload, aggregate_support_fixed_point_reclosure, prepared_source_component_survival, payload_determined_by_declared_read_snapshot, preserved_boundary_sector_map_for_same_boundary_uniqueness. The confluence contract itself is PR-01. Site row consensus.
rows.statement: Transaction read sets contain every finite support whose acceptance can change under the write and are revalidated at commit; enabled repairs in one read/write conflict component commit as one aggregate with one restriction-compatible union-collar payload, and aggregate supports are semantically closed. A prepared aggregate survives disjoint commits, every payload is a function of its declared read snapshot, and same-boundary uniqueness uses the preserved boundary-sector map.

rows.name: Fair-block contraction of noisy repair
rows.summary: Interval Echo has noise-free completion bounds on the routed census: uniform random seam attempts terminate almost surely, and the time to completion is a sum of geometric waits with mean below N(N-1) requests on N ports. Missing: noisy block kernels on the native process and the constants lambda, epsilon, A and beta (theorem thm:noisy-fair-block-consensus, proposition prop:finite-fair-block-certificate). Selection ledger row 9; site row scheduler. The scheduler choice itself is declared architecture.
rows.statement: A noisy asynchronous repair process on the observer-facing quotient has fair blocks of bounded length L that expose and act on every active mismatch class. Each complete block contracts the expected distance D to the exact normal-form set, E[D(B(q))] <= lambda*D(q) + epsilon with 0 < lambda < 1, and within a block E[D(q_t)] <= A*D(q at block start) + beta.

rows.name: Prepared-lock quorum certificate protocol
rows.summary: Finite reference traces execute the protocol as a separate program. Interval Echo has no validators, votes, views or certificates, so the protocol has no native realization. Dictionary members: authenticated_prepared_and_decision_certificates, quorum_certified_prepared_certificate_acceptance_and_lock_propagation, valid_decision_certificate_required_for_finalization, one_supported_value_per_validator_per_view, monotone_view_participation, durable_lock_only_after_assembled_lock_certificate, highest_prepared_certificate_new_view_selection, valid_new_view_supersedes_local_predecision_locks, validator_new_view_justification_check, post_GST_nonfaulty_protocol_progress, quorum_threshold_2q_ge_n_plus_f_plus_1, quorum_availability_q_le_n_minus_f_for_liveness. Site row byzantine. No Lean file states these clauses.
rows.statement: Observers run the raw-prepared, lock and decision certificate protocol: certificates carry a quorum of distinct authenticated votes for one value and view, a nonfaulty validator supports one value per view, never signs for a lower view after entering a higher one, records a durable lock only from an assembled lock certificate before committing, and finalizes only on a valid decision certificate. A new leader proposes the value of the highest valid lock certificate under a checked q-message justification, with quorum thresholds 2q >= n + f + 1 for safety and q <= n - f for liveness.

rows.name: Byzantine fault budget and partial synchrony
rows.summary: Safety uses the fault budget; liveness also uses partial synchrony. The executable model has no fault model, message delay or pacemaker, so neither regime assumption is shown. Dictionary members: at_most_f_Byzantine_validators, partial_synchrony_and_fair_view_change_for_liveness, effective_post_GST_phase_bound. Site row byzantine.
rows.statement: At most f validators behave Byzantine. After global stabilization time one declared bound Theta absorbs route length, per-edge delay, local processing and the fixed message steps of a protocol phase, and once the pacemaker timeout bound is active a fair view change reaches a nonfaulty leader within boundedly many consecutive views.

rows.name: Cell product reading of the screen count (BR-0)

Selection ledger row 7.
rows.statement: The screen record count treats the cells of the screen as independent record carriers, so the count is the product of cell counts (reading (i) of the capacity construction). The alternative reading (ii) refuses the product structure and derives no count.

Record algebras supply the atom readouts of the public sections, every authorized continuation supplies a complete joint checkpoint kernel, the compound confusability graph carries every support-overlap edge with a decoder certificate for M_epsilon(q), refinements create no new confusability, and trial-universe constructors do not expose the expected readback.

rows.name: Native refinement tower of observer and record fibres
rows.summary: Interval Echo realizes the coarse-to-fine algebra maps for protected preparations: a four-child isometry V with V*(I4 ⊗ A)V = A embeds every coarse twelve-address algebra on all 100 parents of the 20→80→320 tower, for both defect signs. Missing: refinement-compatible states and generators for the native free dynamics, which leaves the encoding at first order (transverse derivative at least 1/8 per parent in native time), and observer and record fibres for general preparations. The Lean inhabitants are the constant adaptor constantConsensusTower and one-regulator witness towers; no Lean file in model/ instantiates ConsensusTower.
rows.statement: The native process supplies a nonconstant directed refinement tower. At every refinement level it has finite observer and record fibres, commutative public record algebras inside finite private matrix algebras, one selected density state and one generator per observer, and functorial refinement maps that preserve record order, public algebras, record representatives, state pairings and generators.

rows.name: Regional observer net with access cuts, coverage and descent
rows.summary: The commutation clause on disjoint supports is PR-44; FT-LOCAL demonstrates it for Interval Echo's declared finite operations (all 81 adaptive branches on the 20-owner board preserve every disjoint marginal), and the operational support there does not identify spacelike regions. Regional algebras, access cuts, coverage and descent on Interval Echo records are work in progress. The Lean inhabitants mirror payloads of oph-physics-sim runs b12_prereg_16k_20260806 and e1_prereg2_64k_20260810 with a declared pair-groupoid block adapter; no file in model/ regenerates them. GlueCountermodel proves that ambient unique descent does not imply AccessibleGlueClosure, so both clauses need separate model evidence.
rows.statement: At each refinement level the native process assigns star subalgebras to a finite system of observer regions with isotony, commutation on disjoint regions and state-compatible conditional-expectation restrictions. Each observer has an access cut (a support region and an accessible algebra containing its own records), a region is covered by its declared subregions, and compatible local sections glue uniquely.

rows.name: Operational observers of the native process
rows.summary: Interval Echo patches read sharp material records with a certain immediate reread (FT-RECORD), two owners reread the same physical digit with 32 native branches per order on 20 cells (FT-PROJECTION), and a patch transports its own-history clock to a fixed-home reunion (PATCH-02). Missing: continuation of observer label, readback and prediction across the 20→80→320 tower, a record prediction map, and overlap evidence at more than one regulator. The Lean receipt is fixed-regulator with a finite witness. This row states the content of the site row observer-patch.
rows.statement: Every observer patch of the native process satisfies the seven operational clauses at every refinement level: an accessible algebra containing its public records, a self-readback that fixes its records, records preserved by its persistence generator, record-conditioned interventions that preserve the accessible interface, a non-regressing record prediction map, continuation of label, readback and prediction under refinement, and readable evidence that agrees with an overlapping observer on restricted records.

rows.name: Refinement naturality of native repair, readback and settled endpoint
rows.summary: Replicated protected gates and addressed outcome Kraus operators intertwine with the four-child encoding on all 100 parents of the 20→80→320 tower, so the protected instruments are refinement-natural. Autonomous native flight sends at least 3/16 squared norm per parent out of the code and has a transverse derivative of at least 1/8 for some unit input of every parent, under every choice of child chart, so the free native dynamics fails the same intertwining condition. A settled endpoint branch coherent across the 20-, 80- and 320-cell boards is work in progress. The claim rows record this as cross-regulator realization.
rows.statement: Raw refinement maps between regulators cover the public quotient maps and intertwine the public readbacks, the labelled repair moves and the normalizers. Regional restriction agrees with the natural repair map, and the settled public endpoints form one branch that is coherent under the fine-to-coarse maps.

rows.name: Coherent state on the completed observer colimit
rows.summary: For supplied references, weights and constraints, Interval Echo prepares at each refinement depth a unique relative-entropy minimizer whose four-child projection equals the coarser minimizer (I4/4 ⊗ ρ at fixed coarse marginal ρ), with native records on the 80- and 320-cell boards. That is a projectively compatible family of finite states for one specified construction. Missing: selection from source-derived covers and constraints, the limiting functional and its GNS dynamics on Interval Echo. The Lean instances use a constant witness tower, the two-site Ising benchmark and the eight-history packet of an older source run.
rows.statement: The native process selects a coherent observer family across refinements and a normalized positive functional on the C*-completion of the observer-algebra colimit that restricts to every stage state. Its GNS representation carries the regional algebras and the dynamics used by the QFT attachments.

rows.name: Euclidean cone geometry as the physical field metric
rows.summary: The Lean results hold for the supplied geometry and need no model confirmation as mathematics; the claim rows classify them as non-consumers of registered premises. Interval Echo runs on the spherical 20-, 80- and 320-cell federation, whose carrier is computational hardware with no physical metric (docs/BASIS.md). No test maps Interval Echo records to the cone's Euclidean mass pairings, to a cone refinement, or to sampled fields with the Sobolev bounds that the continuum statements use. Overlaps the continuum-domain and length-scale clauses of PR-53 and is kept separate because it fixes a metric on the cochain cone.
rows.statement: The screen's field sector lives on the 13-vertex, 42-edge, 20-tetrahedron cone over the icosahedral surface with the Euclidean embedding of its vertices. The Whitney edge and face mass pairings of that embedding, and shape-regular refinements of the same cone, are the physical metric and continuum family of the electromagnetic and charged-matter fields.

rows.name: Canonical quantization of the classical field modes
rows.summary: Interval Echo evolves by its native Hermitian generator (FT-FLOW), so its field sector is quantum without a separate quantization step. No result identifies a sector of that generator with the Fock quantization of the Whitney modes. The Planck parameter enters WhitneyQuantumBridge as an input (hbar), which is the calibration of PR-15.
rows.statement: The quantum field sector of the native process is the canonical bosonic quantization, with a positive Planck parameter, of the positive classical normal modes of the declared Whitney field action, so that photon states are occupation states of those modes with energies ħω(n + 1/2).
